findings.claim: Current release-critical artifacts can be regenerated from a clean checkout.
findings.failure_mode: The current checkout is dirty for multiple inspected release-critical artifacts and direct regeneration inputs, including formal/lean/LEAN_BUILD_CERTIFICATE_1_3_3.json, proofs/finite_model_checks/run_finite_model_checks.py, validation/run_all.py, simulations/run_all.py, simulations/adversarial/run_all.py, formal/lean/OC133V12.lean, proofs/finite_model_checks/OC133_FINITE_MODEL_INPUTS.json, simulations/expected_simulations.yml, and tools/materialize_oc_core_1_3_3_v12_closure.py. A clean checkout of the recorded repository state will not contain these exact current bytes, so the release certificate is not currently reproducible from checkout alone.
findings.required_repair: Commit or tag the exact current artifact set, or publish an immutable source archive containing these exact bytes; add a release gate that fails certificate generation when git status is dirty or when required generated outputs are untracked.

findings.failure_mode: The certificate clean_source_manifest omits inspected release-critical entrypoints proofs/finite_model_checks/run_finite_model_checks.py and simulations/run_all.py. The same manifest logic also omits direct simulation inputs such as simulations/expected_simulations.yml and child simulation runners. A clean source copy can therefore pass lake build while being insufficient to regenerate the current finite-model and simulation artifacts, and edits to omitted files do not invalidate the certificate.
findings.required_repair: Make the release-critical manifest complete for all regeneration entrypoints and their direct inputs, including the finite runner, simulation runner, expected simulation file, simulation child runners, validation replay scripts, and numeric replay script; fail if any required ref is absent and record an expected manifest count plus hashes.

findings.claim: The finite-model runner binds current checks to a clean Lean build certificate and reports LEAN_CERTIFICATE_NOT_CLEAN_OR_NOT_BOUND_TO_CURRENT_SOURCE only on drift.
findings.failure_mode: lean_cert_ok checks certificate returncode, theorem counts, current Lean source hash, cache flags, and only that build_transcript_sha256 is nonempty. It does not compare live_lean_build_transcript_sha256, clean_source_manifest_sha256, lakefile_sha256, lean_toolchain_sha256, or generator/template hashes against formal/lean/LEAN_BUILD_CERTIFICATE_1_3_3.json. A stale certificate can survive whenever OC133V12.lean still matches and a fresh lake build succeeds.
findings.required_repair: During the finite-model run, recompute and compare all certificate-bound hashes and the live normalized build transcript hash against the certificate, or regenerate the normalized certificate in the temporary checkout and field-compare it with formal/lean/LEAN_BUILD_CERTIFICATE_1_3_3.json; fail on any drift.

findings.claim: "isolated temp checkout without .lake && lake build OC133V12" demonstrates cache-free reproducibility.
findings.failure_mode: The certificate proves absence of a copied repo .lake directory, but the recorded stderr_tail says the toolchain was already up to date. The build was not isolated from host toolchain state, ELAN_HOME, PATH, or Lake/Lean executable provenance. This supports a no-.lake-cache claim, not a clean-checkout-without-hidden-local-state claim.
findings.required_repair: Run the certificate build in a pinned container or with sanitized toolchain/cache environment, record lean and lake versions plus executable or image digest, and make the certificate distinguish repo-.lake isolation from host toolchain prerequisites.
